video_title: Cynthia Cooper: NEVER Call Out Teammates Publicly + Olivia Miles Has TAKEN OVER In Minnesota

quotes.speaker: Cynthia Cooper
quotes.summary_phrase: Cynthia Cooper criticizes players calling out teammates publicly
quotes.excerpt: I am not a fan of players or coaches going to the media to call anybody out.

text_blocks.speaker: Jordan Robinson
text_blocks.text: Going to the media for coaches and for players is always an interesting thing because, yes, it worked out for Dallas. It also could have not, and everyone could have packed it up and said, I'm out of here, trade me at the trade deadline. But for players, and I'm specifically talking about the Chicago Sky situation and Skylar Diggins, kind of calling out not only her team's effort and starting with herself, but she's saying it starts from the top, the staff. Everybody needs to get on a better page. How do you feel about that and just kind of this in general, being so frustrated that it's spilling over at a post-game press conference?

text_blocks.speaker: Cynthia Cooper
text_blocks.text: I am not a fan of players or coaches going to the media to call anybody out. I can't even imagine me going to a press conference and saying, yo, that's a Van Chancellor question. Don't act like, I don't want to read your mind. Tell me exactly what you want and either I can do it or I can't do it, but at least I know. That's a conversation you have face-to-face, teammate-to-teammate, in the locker room. Hey, let's call a team meeting, let's get in here, let's hammer this out because we want to do better and it's going to start with me. I'm going to lead, and everybody else needs to jump on the same page. So, I'm not a fan of any player calling out their teammates in public.

quotes.speaker: Cynthia Cooper
quotes.summary_phrase: Cynthia Cooper on the mindset of great players
quotes.excerpt: Great players have the ability to focus in on what the goal is.
quotes.quote: Great players have the ability to focus in on what the goal is. And that's the singular most important thing to them in that moment. They don't get messed up with everything that's happening outside the court or around them. They are focused on what they want to achieve and that's the only thing that they're thinking about. And then the other thing is, great players are solution-based. They're looking for solutions to obstacles, to problems. They're not looking to whine or complain, they're only looking at ways to be successful in really anything that they do. And then lastly, I would say work ethic. Great players don't get tired. Great players finish games, finish whatever it is they've decided to do in that moment, they're jumping in with two feet and they are finishers.

quotes.speaker: Cynthia Cooper
quotes.summary_phrase: Cynthia Cooper's favorite memory of winning her first championship
quotes.excerpt: the weight of the world had been lifted off her shoulders and she ran around the court
quotes.quote: I will just say when she won her first championship for UConn. And how excited she was. It's almost like the weight of the world had been lifted off her shoulders and she ran around the court, had her jersey in her hand and was just, UConn, UConn, UConn, UConn. And just running around the court, that was my favorite moment because I know that in that moment, you feel like, yes, it was worth it. The sacrifice was worth it. Traveling across the country was worth it. Mixing in books with school and media and everything, all of the pressure of not just winning games, but winning a championship, that's what she was celebrating. She was celebrating that moment for herself, for her team, and of course the coaching staff.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles' potential as a professional basketball player
quotes.excerpt: we always see the college game through the lens of who's going to be a good pro.
quotes.quote: When we saw Olivia Miles for the first time as a freshman at Notre Dame, right away, because Rebecca and I, because of doing WN Women's College for as long as we have, we always see the college game through the lens of who's going to be a good pro. We right away were like, whoa, Olivia Miles is going to be a great pro.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Notre Dame's underachievement with a talented roster
quotes.excerpt: a team with Sonia Citron and Hannah Hidalgo and Olivia Miles didn't get past the Sweet 16?
quotes.quote: She had success at Notre Dame, but then she tears her ACL, comes back. It was never a perfect fit with Hannah as has been well documented. They kind of underachieve on that team. I think someday we're going to look back and say, wait a second, a team with Sonia Citron and Hannah Hidalgo and Olivia Miles didn't get past the Sweet 16? What?

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cheryl Reeve's unique relationship with her point guards
quotes.excerpt: she really does have this unique relationship with her point guards and empowering them.
quotes.quote: Talking with Cheryl, Angel Gray had to run to do an interview, so she came and she asked Cheryl one question about Olivia right at the beginning of our session with Cheryl. Cheryl talked for 10 straight minutes about Olivia Miles. Angel actually had to leave and go do the interview because she couldn't stay. She was just gushing about Olivia. One of the things I've always appreciated about Cheryl is she really does have this unique relationship with her point guards and empowering them.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles' game is perfectly tailored for the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: Olivia's game is actually perfectly tailored for the W.
quotes.quote: One of the things she talked to us about was how Olivia's game is actually perfectly tailored for the W. The pick-and-roll game is it's so good for Olivia. And she was a little concerned, Olivia was, about the physicality at this level, but as Cheryl told us, she came in at the right time when they're cleaning it up.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Lynx's decision to give Olivia Miles the keys
quotes.excerpt: I was just like, no, we're not doing this two point guard thing. We're giving Olivia the keys.
quotes.quote: Cheryl told us, I was wrestling with this decision we were talking about a staff and I was just like, no, we're not doing this two point guard thing. We're giving Olivia the keys. We have to make a choice here, and she made that choice. Cheryl told us, look, she signed a one-year contract. We're okay with going in this direction.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Liberty's grit and need for improvement
quotes.excerpt: I think I just like their grit right now. I don't think I'm watching them and thinking I'm seeing rhythmic basketball.
quotes.quote: I think I just like their grit right now. I don't think I'm watching them and thinking I'm seeing rhythmic basketball or fluid basketball. Yeah, you know, I think that they have some issues they need to work out. I'm still, you know, you want to see Sabrina back healthy doing her thing. I'm still curious about the fit of Satu and how that's all going to work.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Nyara Sabally's strong play and Liberty front office credit
quotes.excerpt: Nyara is really good. Like, you know, she's a player and I think credit to Jonathan Kolb.
quotes.quote: Nyara is really good. Like, you know, she's a player and I think credit to Jonathan Kolb and the Liberty front office for finding her. And what we're seeing is, and this has been a little bit of a theme that we've talked about, but international players are becoming such critical pieces and there's an influx of them right now in the league.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: WNBA teams must prioritize international scouting
quotes.excerpt: we got to go to international scouting. If you that has not been an area of abundance.
quotes.quote: We got to go to international scouting. If you that has not been an area of abundance in the WNBA and some organizations have been ahead of others. If you are a front office in the WNBA and you want to be serious about competing in this league moving forward, you really have to tap that resource.

quotes.excerpt: for New York right now, for them to be able to tally wins when they're not playing great is significant.
quotes.quote: For New York right now, for them to be able to tally wins when they're not playing great is significant. That was what stood out to me. I didn't watch that game and think like it was it was a hard watch, honestly, like basketball wise that night. The Negroni's helped, but between Indiana and New York, you know, like it was not that was not a fluid basketball game.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Sue Bird's underrated impact on basketball history
quotes.excerpt: I almost think she's become underrated, honestly, in just how great she is in the annals of basketball history.
quotes.quote: Sue has a will to her. Like I I'm just so I almost think she's become underrated, honestly, in just how great she is in the annals of basketball history and what she's accomplished and the all-time winner that she is. And she still just got such a grit and a will.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: New York's ability to win while not playing well

quotes.quote: For New York, tallying wins right now when you're not playing great and then discovering the value of someone like Nyara, really significant stories for them that we're going to track as they they go forward in the season.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Coaching adjustments for the New York Liberty
quotes.excerpt: there's definitely an adjustment to a slightly different system, to some new personnel.
quotes.quote: Especially Sandy had been in New York for a while, right? And so you're used to one coach. You've won with that coach. You've had deep playoff runs with that coach. There's definitely an adjustment to a slightly different system, to some new personnel. But but yeah, I think that's a great point, Allie.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of a new coach on team continuity
quotes.excerpt: some of that blitz to the starting line is affecting the continuity.
quotes.quote: I do think there's some of what we're feeling in the league to start this year and the Liberty are certainly included in this, where there's just like some of that blitz to the starting line is affecting the continuity. And I think it's amplified on a team with a new coach, no question.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the CBA and truncated training camp
quotes.excerpt: it was an insane sprint to the start of the season.
quotes.quote: We were talking to Cheryl about that the other day pregame and she was like, it was an insane sprint to the start of the season. And so I think there's a lot of teams that are still kind of getting their bearings.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Seattle Storm's long-term potential
quotes.excerpt: they're looking at Dominique Malonga and they're thinking, can she be a pillar of a contending team?
quotes.quote: They're looking at Dominique Malonga and they're thinking, can she be a pillar of a contending team in the future, right? They were drafting third this year and whoever they selected, of course, it turned out to be Awa Fam, but they were saying like, can she be the pillar of a championship team in the future? And right now, while they're not going to be good this year and they're going to lose a lot of games, I think it's a really exciting place for the future.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Olivia Miles' game to other stars
quotes.excerpt: there's elements of her game that remind me of Caitlin. She has a different game as far as the shooting goes.
quotes.quote: There's elements of her game that remind me of Caitlin. She has a different game as far as the shooting goes. She doesn't pull up from 35 the way Caitlin does. But they both have some of that kind of just like spice and pizzazz in transition. I think the way she kind of conducts an offense and her vision reminds me a little of Sue and a little of Chelsea. Just in the the kind of like the poise in the quarter court and the control and the mastery and the vision and the conducting and and then the the flare, even within like tight spaces to make some passes.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Olivia Miles' game to Madison Booker
quotes.excerpt: there's elements of Madison Booker's game that remind me of Maya.
quotes.quote: There's elements of Madison Booker's game that remind me of Maya. It's not exactly the same because Maya's a little bit more like moves a little bit more like water than Madison does, but there's elements of how she shoots off the dribble and off curls and stuff that remind me of Maya.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of vulnerability in young players
quotes.excerpt: that vulnerability and the reality of those emotions is strength and it's just part of the human experience.
quotes.quote: I think that's really important for young men to see, you know, because that vulnerability and the reality of those emotions is strength and it's just part of the human experience and, you know, pushing it down is obviously only going to create repressed things that come out in harmful ways. And I just I love his general just embracing of that and and I think it's important for young people to hear because he is the kind of person that they'll listen to.
